description: FULL ACCESS by default: AutoDev works like Claude with full system access — write anywhere, move folders, touch memory, read anything. This is the point. To PROTECT something, add its path to deny_paths (the subtract list) — that's how you tell it what NOT to change. Git and GitHub are never limited by default either (T-37): the force-push wall and the main-tree checkout fuse exist as dials (dangerous_ops.force_push / main_tree_checkout) a shop can turn to "deny" — both ship as "allow". What IS on by default protects the record, not git: deny_paths fences the ledger (.autodev/events.jsonl, tickets, releases) — tracker.mjs is its single writer.

_notes.philosophy: Default is EVERYTHING — including git and GitHub (T-37, owner ruling 2026-08-16: AutoDev never limits what Claude may do in git/GitHub unless the USER limits it — 'it is just Claude doing its own thing'). Restrictions are opt-in per shop: list paths in deny_paths to protect them; set force_push / main_tree_checkout / deploy_or_merge_main to 'deny' to arm those walls. What stays on by default protects the RECORD, not GitHub: the ledger fence (deny_paths on .autodev/events.jsonl, tickets, releases) and worker mode.
_notes.r37: Fuses only for the irreversible class; everything reversible is Claude's own judgment.
_notes.ga37: The ledger (.autodev/events.jsonl) and its authorization artifacts (.autodev/tickets/, .autodev/releases/) are fenced: tracker.mjs is THE single writer (CLAUDE.md invariant), so raw Write/Edit/Bash-append to these paths is denied — closing the re-review's live forged-ledger-line attack (T-19 re-review finding 1, Option A). tracker.mjs's own in-process writes (appendFileSync/renameSync inside the spawned `node tracker.mjs ...` process) are untouched — the guard only ever sees the Bash COMMAND TEXT, never what the process does internally.
